{{ElectionsID}}
he '''2026 United States Senate election in Idaho''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Idaho]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Jim Risch]] is seeking a fourth term. He is being challenged by [[Independent politician|independent]] former state representative [[Todd Achilles]]. 

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 19.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 26, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509222424/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=May 9, 2026|url-status=live|access-date=September 27, 2025|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]}}</ref> Risch won the Republican nomination with 67.3% of the vote, facing minimal opposition. The [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nomination was won by realtor David Roth, who was the nominee in [[2022 United States Senate election in Idaho|2022]], but after Achilles entered the race in July with the support of Democratic leaders, Roth withdrew near the end of the month.<ref name="Roth">{{cite web|url=https://idahocapitalsun.com/2026/07/28/idaho-democrat-david-roth-ends-campaign-for-us-senate-seat-held-by-risch/|title=Idaho Democrat David Roth ends campaign for US Senate seat held by Risch|last=Guido|first=Laura|date=July 28, 2026|access-date=July 28, 2026|website=[[States Newsroom|Idaho Capital Sun]]}}</ref>

Republicans have not lost a Senate race in Idaho since [[1974 United States Senate election in Idaho|1974]].<ref name="IdahoSenators">{{cite web |title=Idaho Senators |url=https://www.senate.gov/states/ID/senators.htm |website=[[United States Senate]] |access-date=October 24, 2026}}</ref><ref name="DemocraticPropsects">{{cite web |last1=Gonzales |first1=Nathan |title=Idaho Senate: Democratic Prospects Still Slim |url=https://insideelections.com/idaho-senate-democratic-prospects-still-slim/ |website=[[Inside Elections]] |access-date=October 24, 2026 |date=August 27, 2007}}</ref>

== Background ==
Idaho is considered a [[red state]].<ref>{{cite web |last = |first = |title = The Road To Red: How One Political Party Came To Dominate Idaho |website = NPR/Bosie State Public Radio |date = |url = https://www.boisestatepublicradio.org/the-road-to-red-how-one-political-party-came-to-dominate-idaho |accessdate = October 21, 2026}}</ref>

This is one of three races (along with [[2026 United States Senate election in Nebraska|Nebraska]] and [[2026 United States Senate election in South Dakota|South Dakota]]) in the [[2026 United States Senate elections|2026 Senate election cycle]] where the Democratic nominee has withdrawn from the race.<ref>{{cite news |last = Shane Goldmacher |first = Shane Goldmacher |title = Democrat Quits Senate Race in South Dakota, Clearing Way for Independent |newspaper = The New York Times |date = August 4, 2026 |url = https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/04/us/politics/julian-beaudion-drops-out-south-dakota.html |accessdate = October 12, 2026}}</ref>

== General election ==
=== Campaign ===
On July 8, 2026, the Ada County Democratic Central Committee sent Roth a letter giving him until August 12 to prove that his campaign "has turned a corner" by raising $50,000 and producing a campaign plan, or the committee would consider endorsing independent candidate Todd Achilles instead. The committee said it was concerned that Roth's campaign was "not positioned to meet the moment” and argued that "we can't afford to let this moment slip away in the best political environment Idaho has seen in decades." Roth called the demands "completely ridiculous" and said he had no intention of complying, while accusing local Democratic leaders of trying to force him out of the race in favor of Achilles.<ref>{{cite news |last=Donovan Smith |first=Orion |title=Idaho They think Jim Risch could be beaten, but they aren't sure they want a Democrat to run for Senate |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/jul/18/idaho-democrats-think-jim-risch-could-be-beaten-bu/ |access-date=July 25, 2026 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=July 18, 2026}}</ref> On July 28, Roth announced he would drop out of the race.<ref name="Roth"/>
